title: Amazon in talks to buy AI startup Decart for around $7 billion, WSJ reports
source_used: SiliconANGLE and CTech (Calcalist), both relaying The Wall Street Journal; Reuters page blocked (HTTP 401)
key_facts: The Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday 11 Oct 2026, citing people familiar with the talks, that Amazon is in talks to acquire Decart for about $7 billion.
A deal could be wrapped up in the coming days, but the talks could still break down or another bidder could emerge.

Decart was founded in 2023 by Israeli engineers Dean and Orian Leitersdorf and Moshe Shalev; its software (DOS) helps AI models run on different processors and cuts chip-specific optimisation from months to a couple of weeks.
Decart raised $300 million at a $4 billion valuation in May, over $400 million in total; investors include Radical Ventures, Nvidia Ventures, Adobe Ventures, Sequoia Capital and Benchmark.

Bloomberg reported last month that Anthropic was in talks to buy Decart for about $6 billion but pulled out after due diligence; the reason is not clear. Nvidia had also pursued a purchase earlier (CTech).
Decart reportedly got early access to Amazon's Trainium3 AI chip in 2025 after AWS engineers were impressed by the founders; AWS is already a customer (CTech).
Decart also builds the Lucy and Oasis world models that generate simulated 3D environments and video in real time.
CTech notes Decart's commercial business is far smaller than the valuation being discussed.
quote_evidence: Amazon.com Inc. is reportedly engaged in discussion over the potential acquisition of artificial intelligence developer Decart.ai Inc. in a deal that could be worth up to $7 billion.

A report in the Wall Street Journal today cites people familiar with the talks as saying that a deal could be wrapped up in the coming days, assuming the discussions don’t break down or another suitor doesn’t emerge.
Amazon is in talks to acquire Israeli-founded artificial intelligence startup Decart for approximately $7 billion, The Wall Street Journal reported Sunday, citing people familiar with the matter.
why_it_matters_hint: Software that moves AI work between chip makers could make Amazon's own Trainium chips easier to use as an alternative to Nvidia.
event_date: WSJ report published 11 Oct 2026; talks ongoing
notes: Reuters original (HTTP 401) and WSJ not opened; text read on SiliconANGLE and CTech, which both credit the WSJ. Amazon has not confirmed. Anthropic walk-away in September is background (reported by Bloomberg, relayed).
